newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran denies its forces involved in northern Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Iran denies its forces involved in northern Iraq.

text.p: Iran rejected accusations that its forces had intervened in fighting between Kurdish factions in northern Iraq, and said it wanted a peaceful solution to the region's problems, Iranian television reported on Sunday.

In a report monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, it said Deputy Foreign Minister Mahmoud Vaezi was speaking to European Union ambassadors, and United Nations and Group of Seven industrial nations representatives.

"The Islamic Republic of Iran's principled policy is based on the preservation of the unity and territorial integrity of Iraq and we strongly reject all accusations that Iranian forces have been meddling in recent clashes in northern Iraq," Vaezi said. He did not name any specific accusations.

"We call for a peaceful solution to the problems of the Kurds, and the Islamic Republic of Iran, in believing that military actions are ineffective in resolving the region's complex problems, has repeatedly demonstrated its good will in helping to resolve the problems of northern Iraq's Kurds, in a peaceful manner, and has taken action in this connection," he was quoted as saying.
Vaezi said the U.S. contravened international conventions and did not act on the basis of United Nations Security Council resolutions when it launched missile attacks on Iraq.
The United States launched 44 cruise missiles last week against southern Iraq after Iraq sent troops into Kurdish areas in its north. Washington also expanded the no-fly zone in southern Iraq.
Iran's President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani has denied U.S. and Iraqi charges of meddling in northern Iraq, saying Iran only targeted its own "anti-revolutionary elements" based there.
